Where building work is carried out in a kitchen or bathroom, any existing fans (including cooker hoods, where they extract to the outside) should be retained or replaced.

The free height from the ground or from the surface of a driveway or walkway of the lower edge of a structural element, device or equipment protruding from the building, such as a balcony, bay window, sign, lighting device or awning, must be at least 2.2 metres, unless the area is protected so as to prevent the danger of collision.
Exits of parts of the building separated by a fire wall must be constructed separately so that in the event of a fire there is no need to use any door that may be in the fire wall.
The use of visually and acoustically reflective wall surfaces should be minimised within the lifting platform to prevent discomfort for people with visual and hearing impairment.
If necessary, fire compartments shall be partitioned in order to restrict the spread of fire and smoke, to provide safe evacuation and to facilitate rescue and extinguishing measures.
The various enduse categories, such as heating, lighting and cooling, should be submetered in such a way that at least 90 of the annual energy consumption of each fuel can be assigned to an enduse.

A sewer installed in the ground shall withstand the load imposed by soil, soil corrosion as well as subsidence of soil.

A glass structure or other light-permeable structure, along with its mountings, must withstand the load to which it is normally subject, unless the structure is protected by a fixed collision barrier.
Generally, gradients within the approach should be as gentle as possible.
The landings in the indoor and outdoor areas of a building must be safe, sufficiently spacious and suitable for their purpose.
Windows, glass walls and glass doors into which there is a danger of collision must be marked in such a way that they can be easily noticed.
The building fabric should be constructed so that thermal bridging, including at the party wall, is reasonably limited.
Ramps, steps, thresholds and differences in levels in passageways must be clearly indicated using lighting and surface brightness contrasts or warning signs.
